pages.title: Pollination
pages.text: A score from 0 to 1 measures the pollinators around a crop: bees, hives, varied flowers, apiaries. Cucumber, strawberry, eggplant and bell pepper need them: without pollinators, their yield drops to 60 %.

pages.title: Biodiversity index
pages.text: Flowers, fruit foliage, bees and hedges raise the index, from 0 to 1. The higher it is, the less disease takes hold. A field surrounded by flowers defends itself better.

pages.title: Flowers and hedge
pages.text: Clover, lavender, chamomile and borage grow in pots or wild. Dyes: clover gives white, lavender purple, chamomile yellow, borage light blue. Hawthorn forms a habitat hedge: 6 leaves and a stick.

pages.title: Insects
pages.text: A butterfly net is made with string. Butterflies, ladybugs and fireflies (at night) inhabit hedges and flowers. Butterfly and ladybug jars keep them.

pages.title: Beekeeping
pages.text: The apiary holds 4 frames and a population of 0 to 100 bees. Empty frames are made from 8 sticks and string. A honey extractor (iron and bucket) and a bee smoker (iron, leather, flint) complete the kit. Honey takes the name of the dominant flower.
